newsitem.title: USA: US administration aims to offer power bill in Feb.
newsitem.headline: US administration aims to offer power bill in Feb.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis said Thursday the Energy Department was aiming to complete its proposals for deregulating the power market by the end of this week so that the whole administration could have legislation ready in February.
The Clinton administration wanted to have a bill ready in time to weigh in when the House started debating the issue, likely in early February, he said.
"We're gearing to a February time schedule," Curtis told reporters after leaving a meeting of a task force on electric system reliability.

Once the Energy Department completes its proposal, it will be debated by several agencies in the administration, including the Environmental Protection Agency, Agriculture and Defense Departments, and several offices in the White House.

The agencies represent a wide range of interests: the Defense Department is the nation's largest energy consumer, and the Agriculture Department has invested $35 billion in rural electric cooperatives.

He said he hoped by filtering the legislation through all the agencies, the administration would come up with a bill representing a broad consensus which might limit confrontation over the issues in Congress.
"This is our nation's most vital industry. It's very, very important we get this transition right," Curtis said.
